title: The status strip is painted directly on top of the record header — the title, NSID and rkey are invisible
evidence: Blogging, record 3l22xtpmjz5p, 1440×1000, unscrolled. Measured: .wb-editor-head rect y=140 h=52; .wb-strip rect y=139 h=53 — identical box. document.elementFromPoint() at the centre of .wb-editor-title (whose text is "Document") returns .wb-strip. Nothing of the header renders: p1-edit.png / p1-preview.png / p1-json.png / s6-aboutrec.png / s7-herorec.png all show an ~83px empty band at the top of the detail pane, then the Save bar, then the tab bar — no record title anywhere. Cause: .wb-strip's sticky inset is `top: calc(var(--chrome-top-h, var(--chrome-h)) + var(--space-3))`. AdminShell withholds ChromeBar on /admin, so --chrome-top-h is never set (getComputedStyle(documentElement).getPropertyValue('--chrome-top-h') === ''), the fallback --chrome-h = 56px applies, and the computed inset is 65.6px. The pane is its own scrollport starting at y=56, so sticky pushes the strip 65.6px DOWN from its natural position (y=73.6) even at scrollTop 0, landing exactly on the header at y=139.
fix: Change `.wb-strip { top: calc(var(--chrome-top-h, var(--chrome-h)) + var(--space-3)) }` to `top: 0`. There is no chrome on this route and `.wb-pane-detail` is the scrollport — the file's own header comment already says "nothing is measured against the chrome any more"; this one rule was not updated. (If a visual inset is wanted, move it to `.wb-pane-detail { padding-top }` so it does not become a sticky offset.)

title: The status strip paints over the pane title and leaves a 66px blank band above itself
evidence:
At 1440 on ?view=nav: .wb-strip computes position:sticky, top:65.6px, z-index:5. Its flow position is y=74 but it renders at y=139–192 — displaced 66px down. The

Nav menu

is at y=140–176, so the overlap is 36px, i.e. the entire heading; document.elementFromPoint over the title returns .wb-strip-state. Result: a 66px band of empty page above a floating "No unsaved changes / Save" bar, and the surface has no visible name. Identical on ?view=publications&r=3lpq72oeo3c2y (strip 139–192, title 140–176, covers:true) and at 1024. Scrolled, it gets worse: the bar pins 66px below the pane's top edge, so live content scrolls in the clear strip above it while the bar cuts the "Use this override" card in half ("The menu below is live on the site." is sliced through at y≈193), and on the publications editor it slices the at:// URI card between its first and last lines. Cause: `top: calc(var(--chrome-top-h, var(--chrome-h)) + var(--space-3))` = 56px + 9.6px, measured against a ChromeBar this route does not render — the comment 250 lines above at adminShell.css:305-307 already says "nothing is measured against the chrome any more — there is no chrome on this route".
fix: In .wb-strip change `top: calc(var(--chrome-top-h, var(--chrome-h)) + var(--space-3))` to `top: 0` (the pane's own padding-top already gives the strip its inset, and the pane's scrollport top IS the frame top). Verify the title is at y=74 again and that the pinned bar sits flush with the top of the pane when scrolled.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: Stacked: the pinned Save bar floats 64px above the bottom of the screen and covers form fields, with live content scrolling in the gap under it
evidence: At 390x844 on ?view=nav the strip renders at y=727–780 with 64px of nothing between its bottom and the viewport bottom, and content visibly scrolls through that band (a whole nav row is drawn under the bar at y≈790–844). It simultaneously covers the "logging" label and "/logging" path inputs by 33px each. Same at 768x900 (strip 786–833, a nav row below it at 855–897) and 320x640. On the publications editor at 390 it covers 41px of the 63px-tall Description textarea; at 768 it also clips the "Show comments" checkbox row; at 320 it hides the middle line of the .pub-uri-hint paragraph, so you read "Paste into src/config.js —" then the bar then "then the site doesn't know this publication exists." Cause: the strip is `bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` but its sticky containing block is .wb-pane-detail's CONTENT box, and the stacked rule gives that pane `padding-bottom: var(--space-8)` = 64px. Overflow clips at the padding box, not the content box, so content shows through the 64px band the bar cannot enter.
fix: Stop the pane's padding-bottom from shortening the strip's sticky rectangle: drop `padding-bottom: var(--space-8)` from .wb-pane-detail in the @media (max-width: 60rem) block and move that bottom breathing room onto the pane's scrolling children instead (e.g. `.wb-pane-detail > .wb-studio, > .wb-editor { padding-bottom: var(--space-8) }`), so the bar pins flush to the frame bottom. Then add scroll-padding-bottom equal to the strip's height so a focused field never lands under it.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: Move up / Move down only ever swaps once — a second press undoes the first, so an entry cannot be moved more than one position
evidence: Order starts [home, themself, available, logging, blogging]. Focus row 0's "Move down" and press Enter three times: [themself, home, ...] → [home, themself, ...] → [themself, home, ...]. It oscillates. Focus (and, for a mouse, the button under the cursor) stays on the DOM slot at index 0, which after the swap belongs to a different entry — so the second press moves the entry that just took its place back up. document.activeElement is still BUTTON.nav-item-btn after each press, i.e. React reuses the element and the entry moves out from under it. Moving "exploring" from position 12 to position 2 is impossible without ten separate re-aims.
fix: After a reorder, move focus to the same button on the row the entry moved TO (keep a ref keyed by entry id and .focus() it in a layout effect after the swap), or key the row elements by entry id so React moves the DOM node with the entry. Either way the control has to follow the item, not the index.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: The signatures list shows a skeleton for ~40 seconds before giving up, with no timeout and no retry
evidence: Timed with a waitForFunction on .feed-empty: page load at 12.8s, the error state finally appeared at 53.3s — about 40s of skeleton after the page was interactive. Screenshots at 1400ms, 16s and 45s all still show five skeleton bars; only the 53s probe shows text. fetchGuestbookEntries has no timeout (grep for timeout/AbortSignal in src/lib/guestbook.js returns only a geolocation call), and status stays 'loading' until every Constellation + per-signer-PDS round trip has exhausted its own network timeouts. The Front Desk's guestbook tile gives up at ~8s, so the same failure reports itself two different ways five times apart. When the error does land it reads "The backlink index is unreachable right now — try again in a bit." with no control to try again — the only way to retry is to leave the surface and come back.
fix: Race the load against an AbortSignal.timeout (~8s, matching the Front Desk tile) in GuestbookModerationPanel.load, and render the error branch with a "Try again" button wired to `load` beside the sentence. src/lib/guestbook.js is read-only per the spec, so both changes belong in the panel.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: The required URL field's placeholder is indistinguishable from a typed value, so an empty publication looks filled in
evidence: On the new-publication form every field is empty, but the URL input reads "https://dame.is/blogging" and looks typed: measured ::placeholder color rgb(46,61,66) (--ink-soft) against a value color of rgb(19,29,32) (--ink) — a contrast ratio of 1.53:1 between the two, with opacity forced to 1 by the reset. In N-pubsnew.png the URL box reads exactly like the filled Name box on the saved record, while the genuinely empty Name and Description boxes below it are visibly blank. This is the one field Save refuses without: PublicationsManager.jsx:437 throws "A publication needs a URL — verification is fetched from it." The Front Desk already flags "2 publications with no url → ADD THE MISSING URLS"; you click through, the box looks like it has a URL, you press Save, and you get a refusal for a field you believed was set.
fix: Either drop the placeholder on this field and let the empty box read empty, or append a `.admin-input::placeholder { color: var(--ink-faint); }` rule (Admin.css is append-only) plus mark the field required and show the "needs a URL" message inline under it rather than only on save failure.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: Two stacked hairlines with a 30px gap of nothing between them, right under the toolbar
evidence: Measured at 1440: .admin-toolbar's border-bottom sits at y=241, .guestbook-entries' border-top at y=271 — 30px apart with no content in between, reading as a doubled rule. Visible at every width (390: y≈310 and 331; 320: y≈338 and 366; 768: y≈332 and 355). The toolbar's rule (Admin.css:138-139, padding-bottom + border-bottom) was a page-level separator; the section's rule (Guestbook.css:126-128, margin-top + padding-top + border-top) was the /welcoming page's separator. Inside one pane they collide. No other surface in the slice has two rules in a row.
fix: Suppress one of them inside the studio — e.g. `.wb-studio > .admin-toolbar { border-bottom: 0; padding-bottom: 0 }` — and let the section's own rule do the dividing. Note Guestbook.css is marked read-only in the spec (shared with /welcoming), so the override has to be admin-side.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: "SIGNATURES" is set at 28px — the same size as the pane title — while the identical kind of label on Site pages is 12px
evidence: Measured: .guestbook-entries-heading computes font-size 28px, letter-spacing 1.4px, all-small-caps, weight 600 — byte-for-byte the same size as .wb-pane-title (28px). Site pages' .admin-collection-group-heading, doing exactly the same job above exactly the same kind of list, computes 12px / 0.6px / all-small-caps / 600. Two sibling studios, one section-label voice, a 2.3x size difference. In the screenshots "SIGNATURES" reads as a second page title competing with "Guestbook" above it, while "LOCAL VS PDS" and "PAGE RECORDS" sit quietly at label scale. The heading has no font-size of its own — it is inheriting the h2 default that made sense when this was the /welcoming page.

file: src/pages/Admin.css (append a .wb-studio .guestbook-entries-heading rule; src/pages/Guestbook.css:131-136 is read-only)

title: No empty state when the last entry is deleted, and the override card then claims a menu that isn't there
evidence: Deleting every row leaves the studio rendering a single bare hairline where the list was, then "+ Add entry · Reset to site defaults" — no copy at all (studio text content is exactly "Nav menu … Use this override The menu below is live on the site. Add entry Reset to site defaults"). The "Use this override" card is still checked and still reads "The menu below is live on the site." when there is no menu below it and saving would blank the site's dock. Nothing warns that an empty enabled override is different from a disabled one.

title: Touch targets far under 44px, worst on the Nav rows where two of them are stacked 20px apart
evidence: Measured inside .wb-pane-detail at 390x844. Nav: "Move up"/"Move down" are 27x20px each and stacked vertically, so the two targets are 20px apart — a thumb cannot reliably pick one; "Hide from menu" and "Remove entry" are 27x27px; the "Use this override" checkbox is 13x13px; "Add entry" 75x22 and "Reset to site defaults" 134x22 (the destructive one). 70 of 70 focusable controls in the Nav pane are under 44px in at least one axis. The 13x13 checkbox needs its whole label row to be the target.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: Focus is dumped to <body>/<main> after every action, and there are 25 tab stops between the top of the page and the pane
evidence: Publications: Tab to a .pub-list-row, press Enter — the editor opens and document.activeElement becomes MAIN.layout. Site pages: click "Migrate to PDS" — the card re-renders and activeElement becomes BODY; same after "Revert to local". Getting back to work then costs the full tab run: from main, "← All publications" is the 26th tab stop (4 top-bar links, then all 21 rail chips, then the strip's Save at 25). The "Skip to content" link lands on main.layout, i.e. before the rail, so it does not skip anything useful.

title: Loading skeletons do not match the content they stand in for
evidence: Publications uses AdminRecordListSkeleton rows=2: measured 35px per skeleton row (a bare 16px bar pair, no frame) against real .pub-list-row cards of 73px each with a 1px border and a background fill — the list grows 83px and gains two card frames when the data lands. Guestbook uses the same skeleton-admin-list markup for signature rows, which are avatar + display name + handle + message + timestamp + a hide control; the skeleton is two flat bars per row on a plain page with no rules. Both are the generic record-list skeleton borrowed for content it does not describe.

surface: /admin?view=pages vs /admin?view=publications (and the pane head on all four)
title: rkeys and NSIDs are set in the serif on some surfaces and in IBM Plex Mono on others
evidence: Measured computed font-family. Site pages: the page-record rkey chips (.admin-record-rkey) render in "Crimson Pro" 12px, and the pane-head NSID chip (.admin-collection-nsid, a <code> element) also renders in "Crimson Pro" 12px — while the <code> two inches below inside the same card renders "is.dame.page/creating" in "IBM Plex Mono" 13.3px. Cause: --mono-ui resolves to var(--font-crimson) (theme.css:65) while .admin-mono uses var(--code); the two are mixed within one row and across two sibling studios.

Given the house rule (IBM Plex Mono for rkeys and at-uris), switch the --mono-ui uses in these admin rules to var(--code).

title: The rkey in a publication row is baseline-aligned to nothing — 9.6px below the title, 16.2px above the URL line
evidence: Measured with a baseline probe inside .pub-list-row: name baseline 286.5, rkey baseline 296.1, url baseline 312.3. The row declares align-items: baseline, but .pub-list-rkey overrides it with `grid-row: 1 / span 2; align-self: center`, so the mono key floats midway between the two lines of the left column. The comparable list one surface over — Site pages' .admin-record-link — measures rkey baseline 2098.8 and title baseline 2098.8, i.e. exactly shared. Two record lists in the same admin, one aligned and one not.

surface: /admin?view=pages → a page record, /admin?view=guestbook → the book record
title: Drilling out of a Site-group studio lands you in a breadcrumb that says "Legacy", with no rail item selected
evidence: Clicking a row in Site pages' "Page records" list goes to ?c=is.dame.page&r=welcoming and the top-bar crumb reads "Front desk / Legacy / Page content / welcoming". Clicking Guestbook's "Edit the book record" goes to ?c=is.dame.guestbook&r=self and reads "Front desk / Legacy / Guestbook (the book) / self". Both were reached from the SITE group, and both NSIDs are registered surfaces. In the screenshot no rail row is marked current, so the one place that tells you where you are tells you "Legacy". Cause: neither NSID has a records-list surface in the registry, so resolveSurface falls through to syntheticSurface(), which hardcodes group: 'legacy' (surfaces.js:499) as "the closest honest bucket for an old NSID you typed in by hand" — but these are not typed in by hand, they are the documented exits from two Site studios.
fix: Give the synthetic surface a neutral group (or omit the group segment from the crumb when surface.synthetic is true) so a hand-opened NSID does not get filed under Legacy, and highlight the originating rail row when the record was reached from a studio.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: Four different gaps between the studio's four top-level groups, because the old page margins are double-counted with the pane's flex gap
evidence: Measured at 1440 down the .wb-studio flex column (gap: var(--space-5) = 17.6px): head→blurb 17px, blurb→toolbar 30px, toolbar→"Local vs PDS" 35px, "Local vs PDS"→"Page records" 66px. The last two are the same kind of break — one top-level section to the next — and differ by 31px. Cause: .admin-page-section carries margin-top: var(--space-7) (48px) and :first-of-type margin-top: var(--space-5), written when this was a full page with no parent gap; flex-item margins add to the gap rather than collapsing, so 17.6 + 48 = 65.6. Visible in the scrolled screenshot as a conspicuous hole between the last page card and the "PAGE RECORDS" label.
fix: Delete the margin-top declarations on .admin-page-section and .admin-page-section:first-of-type and let .wb-studio's gap do the spacing; if the second section wants more air, set it once as a larger gap on that one boundary.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: The editor keeps the list's title and blurb, and re-announces the record in a leftover toolbar row
evidence: Editing "dame is blogging" the pane head still reads "Publications / site.standard.publication" and the blurb still reads "The publications behind the Standard Site embeds." — a list-level description on a detail view. Immediately below, a leftover full-page header row runs "← All publications" on the left and an <h2 class="pub-editor-title"> reading "DAME IS BLOGGING" on the right, measured at 12px — the smallest text on the surface is the name of the thing you are editing, while the 28px heading names the list you left. The top bar already carries "Front desk / Site / Publications / 3lpq72oeo3c2y", so the record is identified in two places, in two forms, neither of them prominent (and the pane title itself is hidden under the strip, defect 1).
fix: Have PublicationsManager pass the selected record's name up so StudioPane's title becomes the publication name with "Publications" as the crumb, and swap the editor blurb for the record-level one. Then the toolbar row only needs "← All publications".
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: The studio's only way back, and its two mode toggles, are drawn as plain prose
evidence: "← All publications", "Edit raw JSON" and "theme only" all compute to color rgb(46,61,66) (--ink-soft), 14px, text-decoration: none, border: none, background: transparent, height 22px. The body copy beside them ("Structured fields cover the essentials…") is rgb(103,124,131) at the same 14px, and the field label above is rgb(74,93,100). So the interactive things are simply the darkest text in the block, with no underline, no accent, no border — while --accent (#0f748a) goes unused on all three. "theme only" sits immediately beside a filled dark "APPLY THEME + AVATAR" button doing a related job and reads as a caption; "Edit raw JSON" at the foot of the form reads as a stray paragraph.
fix: Give .admin-link-subtle a visible affordance — colour it var(--accent) and/or add a 1px underline offset — so a control is never distinguishable from prose by weight of ink alone.
from: Pages, Nav, Publications, Guestbook

title: Unset theme colours render as four solid black swatches
evidence: Neither fixture publication has a basicTheme, yet the Theme row shows four filled pure-black squares labelled Background / Text / Accent / Accent text — on the brand-new publication form too, where every other field is empty. rgbToHex(undefined) returns '#000000' (PublicationsManager.jsx:70-72) and <input type="color"> has no empty state, so "not set" is indistinguishable from "deliberately black", which is also the one value that would break a light embed.

title: "3 records outside the built-in page surfaces" names a count you cannot locate

The Front Desk repeats the same number as an actionable row ("3 page records outside the built-in surfaces → REVIEW THE RECORDS"), which lands here, on the list that will not say which.

title: Two equally weighted primary buttons, one of which silently leaves the admin

The top bar's equivalent, "VIEW SITE", carries an outbound ↗ glyph and an outlined (not filled) treatment; this one carries neither, so nothing warns you that you are about to leave.

title: The sky studio's own Save and Reset buttons are permanently hidden under the fixed hour bar
evidence: With the pane scrolled to its end (1440x1000: scrollTop 981 = scrollHeight 1925 − clientHeight 944, i.e. no further scroll is possible), Save sits at y 896–936 and "Reset 2pm" at y 905–927, while the hour bar's top edge is y 860. elementFromPoint at the centre of Reset returns BUTTON.sky-arc-cell — clicking where Save/Reset are drawn changes the previewed hour instead. Identical at 1024x800 (bar y 660, 76px covered), 768x1024 (bar y 884), 390x844 (bar y 708, Save y 739–780) and 320x568 (bar y 432, Reset y 473–495). Arithmetic: the bar occupies 84px + a 56px bottom offset = 140px of the pane, and .wb-pane-detail reserves padding-bottom: var(--space-8) = 64px, so 72–76px of content is unreachable at every width. The studio registers no .wb-strip, so this IS its only Save.
fix: Two changes. (a) .sky-hourbar uses `bottom: calc(var(--chrome-h) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))` — correct on the public site, wrong in the admin, which draws no ChromeBar; under the admin shell it must be `bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)`. (b) The studio already measures itself into --sky-hourbar-h (SkyThemeStudio.jsx:174) but only .app-shell consumes it; add `.wb[data-surface='sky'] .wb-pane-detail { padding-bottom: calc(var(--space-8) + var(--sky-hourbar-h, 0px)) }`.
from: Sky, Ratioed studio, Ratioed catalogue, Legacy blogs, Listening

title: The hour bar spans the whole viewport and makes the last rail links unclickable
evidence: The bar is position:fixed with left:0;right:0, so at 1440x1000 its rect is x 0–1440 — it lies across the 216px rail. "Legacy blog migration" (y 856–889) and "Created work (legacy)" (y 893–926) both hit-test to DIV.sky-hourbar, and the rail cannot be scrolled out from under it there (.wb-rail-scroll scrollHeight === clientHeight === 861). At 1024x800 the rail does scroll, but even at max scrollTop the last item lands at y 707 under a bar whose top is y 660, and hit-tests to BUTTON.sky-arc-cell. Independent proof: Playwright's click on a[href*="view=legacy-blogs"] retried for 30s and failed with `<div class="sky-hourbar"> intercepts pointer events`. While sky is open, the Legacy group is unreachable from the rail at every desktop height tested (1000, 800, 700).

Measured computed font-family: Site pages' .admin-record-rkey chips ('welcoming', 'blogging', 'creating') render Crimson Pro 12px, while the SAME rkeys in the generic record-list pane (.wb-list-rkey at ?c=is.dame.page) render IBM Plex Mono — two lists of the same records, two fonts. Working fix: hoist the token — `:root[data-admin-shell] { --wb-rail-w: 13.5rem }`, have .wb-shell consume it rather than declare it, then `:root[data-admin-shell] .sky-hourbar { left: var(--wb-rail-w) }`, with `left: 0` restored inside the existing max-width: 60rem block where the rail becomes a top chip row.

surface: Record detail, a record that does not exist — /admin?c=is.dame.now&r=doesnotexist
title: A missing record renders an editable form with Save armed; pressing Save creates the record
evidence: Drove it with Playwright: loaded /admin?c=is.dame.now&r=doesnotexist, clicked Save in the strip, and the list immediately gained a row '(untitled) · doesnotexist · just now' (42 → 43 rows). getRecord threw, RecordEditor set `error` and cleared `loading`, so the form paints empty and interactive; handleSave takes the `isNew === false` branch straight to putRecord with the typo'd rkey and writes a status record with no status text into the public is.dame.now collection. Delete is enabled too. The only sign anything is wrong is a 12px line BELOW the last field reading 'Could not locate record: is.dame.now/doesnotexist' — a raw PDS message with no fix in it. Cmd+S does the same thing (AdminShell's key handler only checks saving/deleting/loading).
fix: Give the editor a `notFound` status distinct from `error`, and render a real state instead of a form: 'No record at is.dame.now/doesnotexist — it may have been deleted.' with 'Back to Logging' and 'Create it at this key' as explicit choices. RecordDetail must call registerActions(null) (or pass save:null, canDelete:false) when the load 404s, so the strip offers nothing.

title: Create writes a record with every required field empty, with no validation and no error
evidence: Clicked 'New' on Blogging and then 'Create' without typing anything. The button was enabled (isDisabled → false); the write succeeded; the URL patched to &r=3l223o25uetli and the list's top row became '/3l223o25uetli · 3l223o25uetli · just now' — a site.standard.document with no title and no publication, whose path is its own rkey. TITLE and PUBLICATION are both drawn with the required asterisk, so the asterisk is decorative: handleSave never inspects lex.fields[].required before calling createRecord. The strip then reads 'No unsaved changes', so nothing on screen says a junk record now exists.
fix: Pre-flight the write: collect `lex.fields.filter(f => f.required && isEmpty(value[f.key]))`, and if any are empty refuse to save, name them in the strip ('Title and Publication are required'), and move focus to the first empty one. Never let a required-field violation reach the PDS.

title: The Front Desk skeletons are far shorter than the content, so the surface grid jumps 225px when they resolve

surface: Record detail save strip — every ?r= surface
title: The pinned Save/Delete bar sits 64px off the bottom edge, with live form fields scrolling through the gap underneath it

surface: Record list → record → back, any collection
title: Drilling into a record and coming back resets the list to the top and drops focus into <main>
evidence: Scrolled `.wb-pane-list` to scrollTop 1400 of scrollHeight 3144 (a 42-record Logging list), tapped the row at y=329 ("not answering email"), then clicked "← Logging". Result: `listScrollTop: 0`, 42 rows freshly rendered. `document.activeElement` is `layout MAIN` both after the tap and after the back — focus is never placed on the record heading, and never returned to the row you came from. Cause: AdminShell unmounts the non-visible column when stacked (`showList = isList && (!stacked || column === 'list')`). On a phone that is the single most-repeated gesture in the admin, and it is the exact promise the rebuild's header comment makes ('the list column keeps its scroll position').
fix: Keep both columns mounted when stacked and hide the inactive one (`display: none` / `hidden` + `inert`) rather than unmounting, so the list's scrollTop survives; then move focus to the detail pane's `<h1>` on drill-in and back to the originating row's link on drill-out.

surface: Record detail, any surface with a text field
title: The iOS keyboard will sit on top of the pinned save strip — the shell is bound to the layout viewport, not the visual one
evidence: `.wb` measures exactly `innerHeight` (844 = 844) with `position: fixed; inset: 0` — i.e. the LAYOUT viewport. adminShell.css:63-65 claims '`inset: 0` on a fixed element is the visual viewport, which is what the iOS keyboard shrinks'. This project's own `src/hooks/useKeyboardInset.js` documents the opposite in its header: 'a mobile keyboard doesn't shrink the layout viewport it's pinned to — it just covers it… a sheet hosting a text field therefore ends up *behind* the keyboard.' BottomSheet and ActionDock both consume that hook; the admin shell does not, and the viewport meta is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover` with no `interactive-widget=resizes-content`. NOTE: established from code + measurement, not from a screenshot — headless Chromium has no software keyboard, so I could not photograph the occlusion.
fix: Either add `interactive-widget=resizes-content` to the viewport meta, or apply the existing `useKeyboardInset` in AdminShell and publish it as `--wb-kb-inset`, subtracting it from `.wb`'s height and adding it to `.wb-strip`'s bottom offset — the same compensation ActionDock already performs.

title: 21 chips in a 3034px horizontal scroller: 7.8 screens of swiping, no group structure, no scroll cue
